summary: Jörundur Garðar Hilmarsson (1946–1992) was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at the University of Oslo (M.A.), the Sorbonne, under Werner Winter, and earned a Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1982–1986). He taught at the University of Iceland (~1987–1992).

Jørn Borup (1966–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Aarhus University (~1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, later serving there as Associate Professor (~2006–2023).

Júlia Szivák works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Corvinus University, Eötvös Loránd University, Central European University, and earned a PhD at Birmingham City University (2017–2021). She held posts at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Nottingham.

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who studied at Munich, Bochum, Bonn, and Marburg (PhD ~1992–1996) under Michael Hahn and Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Bonn, the University of Halle (~1999–2007), and became Professor at Marburg in 2007.

Jürgen Neuß is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin by 2007, where he was also attested between 1998 and 2008.

Jürgen Renn is a historian and philosopher who studied at FU Berlin, Sapienza, and TU Berlin (Ph.D. ~1983–1987). His posts include Boston University, Director at MPI for the History of Science (1994), and Director at MPI of Geoanthropology (2022).

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri (1892–1975) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras (~1909–1913). He held posts at Annamalai University, the University of Madras (~1929–1946), and the University of Mysore (~1952–1956).

K. A. Subramania Iyer (1896–1980) studied under Sylvain Lévi, Lionel David Barnett, and at the universities of London and Paris. An Indologist, linguist, and philosopher, he served as Professor at the University of Lucknow (1921–1960) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Ammini Amma is an Indology scholar who was attested as a research student at the University of Madras in 1940 and 1971.
K. Balasubramania Iyer (1892–1970) was an Indology scholar who served as Managing Editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and Secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).
K. Jayakumar is an Indology and linguistics specialist who studied at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School, Thiruvananthapuram, and served in the Indian Administrative Service from ~1978 to 2012.
K. Kanapathypillai (1902–1968) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Hartley College and the University of London (~1934–1936).

K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) studied under C. Kunhan Raja, Thomas Burrow, and John Brough, earning PhDs at Madras and London. An Indologist and linguist, he headed Sanskrit at the University of Madras and advised the Adyar Library (~1971–2005).

K. L. Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yinshun, at the University of Kelaniya, and under Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya (~1986–2003) and served at the University of Hong Kong (~2004–2014) and Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indology scholar who studied under C. Kunhan Raja. He was affiliated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940, 1971) and served as Curator of the Anup Sanskrit Library (attested 1946).

K. Meenakshi is an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed a Doctor of Philosophy under M. A. Mehendale at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964. She held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. Munirathnam is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy and served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2013–2018).

K. N. Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under O. H. de A. Wijesekera, Ludwig Wittgenstein, and at the University of Cambridge, later serving as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (~1952–1963).

K. N. Neelakantan Elayath is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Government Arts College (1967–1969), Sree Krishna College (1972–1984), and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calicut (1990–2003).

K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, and held posts in Cambridge's Faculty of Oriental Studies (1954–1992) and the Pali Text Society (1959–2010).
